Purpose
-------
Clear or normalise the repository `CHANGELOG.md` that was copied from the template.

Prerequisites
-------------
- Local clone with `origin` set and write access.
- `git` available.

Dry-run recommended
-------------------
List the file and show first and last 20 lines before editing:

```powershell
git fetch origin --prune
git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard -- "CHANGELOG.md"
if (Test-Path CHANGELOG.md) { Get-Content CHANGELOG.md -TotalCount 20; "..."; Get-Content CHANGELOG.md -Tail 20 }
```

Non-destructive (recommended)
----------------------------
Replace the file with a minimal header and commit the change:

```powershell
if (Test-Path CHANGELOG.md) {
  @"
# Changelog

> This changelog was cleared during repository initialisation. Add release notes here following Keep a Changelog.
"@ | Out-File -Encoding utf8 CHANGELOG.md
  git add CHANGELOG.md
  git commit -m "chore: clear template changelog"
  git push origin HEAD
} else { Write-Host "No CHANGELOG.md found; nothing to do." }
```

Destructive (clear file contents but keep tracked)
------------------------------------------------
```powershell
if (Test-Path CHANGELOG.md) {
  "" | Out-File -Encoding utf8 CHANGELOG.md
  git add CHANGELOG.md
  git commit -m "chore: remove templated changelog content"
  git push origin HEAD
}
```

Notes
-----
- This operation creates a commit that will appear in repository history; you can amend or squash later if desired.
- If you prefer to remove the file entirely, use `git rm CHANGELOG.md` instead — only for repos that do not require a changelog file.
